messages.author: d0bb2cbcd3025fd1
messages.subject: IRT with covariates
parts:
Hi Phil, 

I have a question about adding covariates into an IRT model. 

Let's say I plan to add gender as a construct level covariate (theta~gender) for a unidimensional 2PL model and the effect of gender tends to be quite large (e.g., R2 = 0.60). In this case, are item parameters from the model with covariates different from those from the model without covariates due to the scaling?  In the model without covariates, the variance of theta is fixed to one for identification. But in the model without covariates, I assume that it is the residual variance that is fixed to one. If that's the case, is there a way to convert these parameters to the same metric so that we can compare them? 

The reason why I ask this question is that I am running a simulation to see whether adding covariates can improve parameter estimation. But I found that item parameters from the model with covariates deviated substantially from the true parameters despite that person parameters are more accurately estimated. It is very surprising to me. Therefore, I suspect it should have something to do with scaling. 

Thank you very much! 

Best,
Bo

messages.subject: Re: IRT with covariates
parts:
On Fri, Mar 5, 2021 at 11:41 PM Bo <bobby1...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Phil, 

I have a question about adding covariates into an IRT model. 

Let's say I plan to add gender as a construct level covariate (theta~gender) for a unidimensional 2PL model and the effect of gender tends to be quite large (e.g., R2 = 0.60). In this case, are item parameters from the model with covariates different from those from the model without covariates due to the scaling?  In the model without covariates, the variance of theta is fixed to one for identification. But in the model without covariates, I assume that it is the residual variance that is fixed to one. If that's the case, is there a way to convert these parameters to the same metric so that we can compare them?

Yes, and indeed for any model that doesn't freely estimate the variance of the latent trait you should consider changing the identification to the version where the latent variable scale is determined by an item (say, item 1) by freeing the latent trait variance parameter and setting the slope of the identification item to 1. This is actually the default in most SEM software, precisely for this reason. 

Because this is a simulation study just be careful about the scaling of the item parameters and traits. I often will just generate data given that the first item slopes is always fixed at 1, and change the latent variance and remaining parameters through the simulations. HTH.

Phil

The reason why I ask this question is that I am running a simulation to see whether adding covariates can improve parameter estimation. But I found that item parameters from the model with covariates deviated substantially from the true parameters despite that person parameters are more accurately estimated. It is very surprising to me. Therefore, I suspect it should have something to do with scaling. 

Thank you very much! 

Best,
Bo
